title: Threshold accepting in the reinsertion loop
spec: Change the acceptance rule of the remove-and-reinsert loop from strict improvement to threshold accepting. Accept a candidate packing if its sum of radii after _repair is at least the incumbent's sum minus a threshold tau, where tau starts at 0.004 and decreases linearly to 0 over the loop. Always keep a separate copy of the best packing found so far, and return that copy at the end, so the loop may drift through slightly worse states without losing the best. Everything else stays the same, including the random-restart phase and the reinsertion move.

title: Sequential LP with trust region
spec: Add a sequential linear programming polish as an alternative to SLSQP for the reinsertion loop. At the current (c, r), linearise every pair-distance constraint d_ij - r_i - r_j >= 0 and the wall constraints around the current point. Solve scipy.optimize.linprog (highs) for a step that maximises sum(dr) subject to |dc|, |dr| <= delta. Accept the step if the true constraints (nonlinear) are satisfied or the objective improves, and otherwise shrink delta by half. Grow delta by 1.5 after successful steps. Run until delta < 1e-7 or the time is up, then apply _repair. Use this only in the reinsertion loop; keep SLSQP for the random restarts.

title: Elite alignment and crossover via assignment
spec: Keep the top two packings from the random-restart phase. Before crossover, align the second packing to the first with scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment on the matrix of pairwise centre distances, so that circle indices correspond. Build a child by taking the centres and radii of the first elite for circles in one half-plane (x < a random cut x0 drawn from [0.3, 0.7]) and the aligned second elite for the rest. Repair the child, run _optimise on it, and then repair again. Keep it if its radius sum beats the incumbent. Use this crossover as an extra move alongside remove-and-reinsert, chosen with probability 0.3.

title: Tabu memory of failed reinsertion sites
spec: In the reinsertion loop, keep a list of the positions where the removed circle was reinserted in previous steps that did not improve the packing, together with the radius of the removed circle. When choosing a new position for the smallest circle, draw 200 uniform candidate points in [0,1]^2 and discard any candidate within 0.08 of a stored failed site. Take the candidate with the largest distance to its nearest centre among the remaining points. Clear the tabu list whenever an improvement is accepted. This steers reinsertion toward unexplored holes and avoids repeating the same unsuccessful moves.

title: Weighted-radius objective for basin diversification
spec: In _solve_once, draw a random weight w_i in [0.5, 1.5] for each circle and minimise -sum(w_i * r_i) instead of -sum(r_i) in _optimise. The constraints stay unchanged. Weights change which basin SLSQP falls into. After this solve, run one unweighted _optimise call from the resulting point to restore the true objective, then call _repair as before. The restart selection rule is unchanged.

title: Exact LP radius polish for fixed centres
spec: After each SLSQP solve, freeze the centres and solve the linear programme maximise sum(r) subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij for all pairs and r_i <= distance of c_i to each wall, using scipy.optimize.linprog (highs). This gives the optimal radii for those centres exactly and replaces the heuristic radius shrinking in _repair, so less sum is lost to repair.

title: Incremental growth from k to n circles with warm starts
spec: Instead of random starts at n=26, grow the packing from small size. Start with k=4 circles at random, optimise with _optimise, then insert one new circle at the centre of the largest empty region (sample 2000 random points and pick the one with the largest distance to all centres and walls) with radius 0. Re-optimise with _optimise. Repeat until n circles are placed. Use this growth path for a share of the restarts (about half of the random-restart phase, with different seeds for the insertion sample). Keep the best complete packing by radius sum as the start for the remove-and-reinsert loop.
